bullets.text: CR 93.6 beat the 96 target; April and May averaged close to 92, while June produced 97, in part reflecting Midwest flood losses; no state presented a disproportionate profitability concern.

Catastrophe response teams deployed 19 separate times during Q2, exceeding the prior full-year record of 15 in 2005; over 20,000 catastrophe claim features were reported, with about 95% closed within 30 days.
Companywide NPW fell ~1% YOY; PL fell 1% (Agency -3%, Direct +3%); CL fell 5%; earned premium per earned car year declined across all sectors: auto -5%, Special Lines -6%, and CL -9%.

Companywide PIF +3% YOY; Agency auto -2%, Direct auto +7%, Special Lines +8%, Commercial Auto +4%; all Personal Lines retention measures improved significantly, with several approaching all-time highs.

Reduced driving from high gas prices supports speculation of falling accident frequency; the previous outlook for rate increases to match bodily injury inflation is now less clear, amid likely mix shifts toward smaller cars.

Executed more than one auto rate revision per business day; smaller declines in written premium per car year than earned premium reflect rate actions, serving as a leading indicator of future earned levels.

Entered Massachusetts on May 1st with Internet auto quoting, adding 12,000+ customers; the Internet was the most positive new business source, while Agency new business was lower and New York and California saw reductions.

Expanded usage-based insurance program with prominent national media coverage; introduced a 'name your price' shopping concept to be tested in Q3, with both initiatives demonstrating appeal across different consumer segments.

Classified $43M of unrealized losses as other-than-temporary during Q2; Progressive will maintain conservative portfolio management and accounting of impairments amid concerning investment market instability.

Published 2007 industry data showed private passenger auto written premium was flat, marking a third consecutive year under 1% growth; commercial auto suggested a 4% decline after two years of near-zero growth.
